key_insight: WildWorld provides a large-scale, action-rich dataset where actions are tied to explicit latent states (not just pixels), enabling learning of action-conditioned latent dynamics for more accurate generative and planning models.
problem_solved: Existing video/world-model datasets lack diverse, semantically meaningful action spaces and do not separate visual observations from the underlying state dynamics, limiting training of action-conditioned latent models.
method: Curate a large-scale dataset with temporally aligned triples: explicit latent states, semantically meaningful actions, and corresponding visual observations.
Annotate and structure the data so actions operate on latent states (state transitions) rather than directly on pixels, enabling supervised learning of action-conditioned dynamics.
Provide benchmark tasks and metrics (state prediction, action-conditioned video generation, planning/generalization) to evaluate generative world models and ARPG-style agents.
impact: WildWorld fills a crucial data gap for training and evaluating action-conditioned latent dynamics, accelerating research in world models, model-based RL, and generative agents for complex interactive environments.
visual_elements: Diagram: latent-state → action → next-latent-state pipeline with separate visual observation arrow (shows decoupling of state and pixels)

paper_title: WildWorld: A Large-Scale Dataset for Dynamic World Modeling with Actions and Explicit State toward Generative ARPG
paper_authors: Zhen Li, Zian Meng, Shuwei Shi, Wenshuo Peng, Yuwei Wu
